agreement.rule: D19's proposal (labeler builder:refcheck+regression+construction:v1) against the second labeling, each distinct graded patch once (a unit's label is its members' when they agree, else ambiguous); the 2x2 table holds the units both label valid or invalid, the cross-table every unit (none: no D19 proposal, or not graded by the labeler); per task family (case-study mode, §19.6: no pooled agreement) (§15.4 estimand 4, §15.5)

independent_labeling.natural_rule: a pass on a natural pre-review state (origin natural_pre_review) is ambiguous, as D19's natural rule makes it: the correction is not observable by the checks (D64); the pre-review states existed before the labeler was written, so the agreement on them is marked as such (§15.5); a task whose labeler the run graded and whose verifiers/independent_label/status.json does not record the status usable is left out of the second labeling and reported
independent_labeling.primary_labels: D19's proposals, or a human label where one exists (the label rule of the primary analysis)
independent_labeling.rule: the independent labeler (verifier independent_label, condition reference_check; protocol §15.5) labels a candidate valid if it passes, invalid if it fails with task_failure, and ambiguous on any other outcome (unresolved, environment failure, verifier error or timeout, recorded as such); a candidate it did not grade is unlabeled. Its verdicts are a second labeling (§15.4): a model proposal, as D19 is, never a human label. The labeler is label support, never an evaluated condition

ambiguous_reasons.NP-03-eval-nm-1: construction invalid but reference checks and regression norm pass

ambiguous_reasons.NP-05-eval-nm-3: construction invalid but failing checks map to other requirements

ambiguous_reasons.NP-20-eval-nm-3: construction invalid but reference checks and regression norm pass

case_study.omitted: every pooled rate with its exact and bootstrap intervals (conditions is empty), every paired comparison with its p-values (comparisons is empty), the bootstrap appendix, and every pooled sensitivity table; each is given per family instead
case_study.rule: protocol §20.3 (§19.6, §15.6): each natural run is reported on its own, so the size threshold counts the run's own accepted tasks (its families accepted, S11, in the committed index), not the accepted tasks of both samples; with fewer than 10, the run's tasks are exploratory case studies, reported in per-family tables only, with no pooled rate, interval or p-value; with 10 or more, §15.6 and §15.7 apply in full to the run, and each task's sample is reported. Only a combined report over both runs applies the threshold to their union
case_study.why: the run grades 6 accepted task(s) of its own (its families accepted, S11, in the committed index), fewer than 10; each run is reported on its own (protocol §20.3)

label_support.rule: label-support verifiers (condition reference_check: the reference checks and the independent labeler) are never evaluated conditions; their results are kept apart from the conditions' rows (D19, protocol §15.5)

reporting_rules.basis: the run was graded with tc-harness/0.3.5, and new runs use tc-harness/0.3.5 or later (protocol §16.1)
reporting_rules.protocol: experiments/protocol.md v0.7 §15.7 and v0.8 §16.6, in case-study mode (v0.11 §19.6, v0.12 §20.3)

secondary_conditions.rule: B3 (diff_derived) is a secondary arm of the natural PR-review arm (protocol §15.6): its rates, per-family table and paired comparisons are reported here, apart from the primary conditions, and its comparisons stay out of the primary null tally

natural.construction_rule: per family, from its task directory (D64; the counts of D70): each contract's requirements, active ones and scored active ones (the reference contract's also at the correction: its correction requirements); the checks of each registered verifier, by condition (the label-support verifiers by id); the audit of C2 and C4 from each spec's audit record (whether it passed, its revisions, the finding codes of its last iteration; never a finding's message); whether B3 is available (a registered B3 spec, else why not); and the reference checks' status record (verifiers/reference_check/status.json: whether a readable record exists, its status, usable or unusable, and its fix rounds, an integer fix_rounds; usable is null without a readable record holding one of the two statuses, fix_rounds is null without that integer, and why says which). Ids, counts and codes only

cost.rule: per family: the generation records of its generated artifacts (contracts, verifiers other than B1, constructed candidates; a combined record sums its runs), its S10 record's time from built_at to passed_at and its base-test run, the S10 fetch log's bytes of the family's repository (a repository's fetches include those made for any family of it) and the run's grading time (the sum of each pair's wall time); the totals over the run's families, and each total divided by their number (per accepted task, when the run grades every accepted family of its sample: see the index check); a total is n/a when a family lacks the value. S10's cost per accepted task counts its time and its fetches on one basis, the S10 work of every family S10 processed, both samples, rejected families included (s10_every_family: the time from built_at to passed_at or rejected_at; every S10 fetch in the log, its bytes and seconds), divided by the same number; the run's families' own S10 time (s10_seconds_run_families) and their repositories' fetches are given beside it

not_recorded.NP-07: rejected during the build: its task directory keeps only rejection.json, which records the rejection's time and no start
not_recorded.NP-08: rejected during the build: its task directory keeps only rejection.json, which records the rejection's time and no start
not_recorded.NP-12: rejected during the build: its task directory keeps only rejection.json, which records the rejection's time and no start

s10_every_family.rule: every family S10 processed, both samples, accepted and rejected: a family with an S10 record (s10.json, or the rejection.json of a family rejected during the build) under the tasks root, or one the committed index records with an S10 outcome; its time runs from built_at to passed_at or rejected_at. processed_not_in_index: families with an S10 record whose row in the committed index records no S10 outcome (or that have no row), whose work is counted as their fetches are

unrecorded: stages S1 to S9: the funnel queries, the S9 fetches and the S9 judges' agent runs (their records are kept outside the repository)
S10 re-runs after compiler fixes (D59): s10.json keeps the times of the last build only, while the fetch log keeps every fetch
the S10 compile step's time before built_at (resolving the commits, materialising the base and the candidates), apart from its fetches, whose seconds the log records: s10.json records no start of it
image builds and wheel downloads, apart from the wheelhouse bytes that s10.json records
the host's own steps (D24): workspaces, builds, audits, freezing and labelling, apart from the run's grading time
agent runs that leave no generation record: the mappers, the optional construction checkers and any run before a re-run

the S10 time of NP-07, NP-08, NP-12, left out of the S10 time of every processed family: rejected during the build: its task directory keeps only rejection.json, which records the rejection's time and no start
the S10 time of NP-35, left out of the S10 time of every processed family: its s10.json records no end (outcome 'built')
the time of 1 S10 fetch(es) of the log, which record no seconds (their bytes are counted)

natural.d19_rule: labels.<task>.d19, for a natural run only: D19's proposals (labeler builder:refcheck+regression+construction:v1) for the task's held-out candidates, the reference and the no-op left out as in counts, with every value counted, zero included (unlabeled: no D19 proposal); and, for each candidate that D19 labels ambiguous, the category of its reason, read from the head of its label's note, where scripts/propose_labels.py writes the reason (its d19 and combine_repeats; decision log D19, D64): the reason itself where it is one of D19's fixed reasons for an ambiguous label; 'the repeats give different proposals: a missing decision' where the repeats disagree, whatever proposals the reason lists; 'no reason recorded' for a note that holds none; and 'unrecognised reason' otherwise, with nothing of its text. Ids and categories only; the candidate files read are hashed in meta.inputs

rejected.NP-07: base tests: the base-test subset is empty (no test file imports a changed module, the PR changes no test file present at the base, and the changed package has no test directory) (§17.2)
rejected.NP-08: fetch over the caps (§15.6): git fetch stopped: the clone went over the repository cap of 300000000 bytes
rejected.NP-10: no resolvable closure: no wheels-only resolution
rejected.NP-12: a merge between the base and the addressing commit changes the commented file (§15.6)
rejected.NP-13: no resolvable closure: an sdist-only requirement is not pure Python
rejected.NP-15: environment too large: the wheelhouse would hold 3.15 GB, over the 1.5 GB cap (§17.1)
rejected.NP-16: no resolvable closure: pip's resolver did not finish within 30 minutes
rejected.NP-17: no resolvable closure: pip's resolver did not finish within 30 minutes

funnel.rule: S1 to S8a: the deterministic screen (D48); S9: the model judges per sample (§15.6, §19.2); S10: replayability per sample, with each rejection's reason (§15.6, §17); S11: accepted, that is passing S10 within the family cap (§16.4); counts only, from the records named

index.rule: protocol §20.2: each natural run grades the accepted families of its sample (natural-pr-v1 the first sample's, natural-pr-v2 the extension's), so the run's families are checked against the accepted families (S11 in the committed index) of the samples their index rows name; accepted families of another sample are not the run's
index.source: data/manifests/natural_tasks_index.json at the run's code revision e9c9c91450c0

records.rule: read as the commit that the run's manifest records (code_revision) holds them, the records the run's acceptance gate read; a later commit of the index changes nothing here

reliability.rule: per family: the S10 record, the reconstruction record, the task image's id as the run, snapshot.json and s10.json record it, the run's grading of the reference and the no-op by every verifier (label support included), and the pairs whose three repeats disagree (unresolved, counted as a rejection, §15.3) or that ended in an infrastructure outcome (environment failure, verifier error or timeout; an unresolved pair is counted as unresolved only)

natural.rule: natural PR-review arm (protocol §15.6, §17, §19): per family, its sample, whether B1 is available (s10.json) and whether its overlay equals D19's regression norm (labels/base_tests_overlay, by file), the correction requirements (the reference contract's scored active requirements introduced at the review comment or one of the reviewer's replies; D64, decision 14), the held-out near misses that name one in their construction label, and its construction facts (contract counts, checks per verifier, the audits of C2 and C4, whether B3 is available, the reference checks' status record; construction_rule); the funnel S1 to S11 of both samples with reasons; build and replay reliability; and cost and time per accepted task. Ids, outcomes, counts and hashes only

oracle_gated.rule: a verifier x task cell is dropped when the verifier does not pass the task's reference solution in the run's sanity grading; its held-out candidates are the lost yield (secondary view, protocol §15.7); per family only (case-study mode, §19.6)

secondary.rule: B3 (diff_derived) is a secondary arm of the natural PR-review arm (protocol §15.6): its rates, per-family table and paired comparisons are reported here, apart from the primary conditions, and its comparisons stay out of the primary null tally

source_evidence.banner: source evidence, not a human label: the reviewer's request, the addressing commit and the agreement of both S9 judges label each pre-review state invalid with respect to the correction (protocol §15.6)
source_evidence.case_study: per-family tables only: no pooled count, rate or p-value (protocol §19.6)
source_evidence.rule: labeler kind source_evidence: the reviewer's request, the addressing commit and the S9 agreement; reported apart from D19 and never a human label (protocol §15.6)
